Patch 0.41.0.1 (the Lanternhold oathguard)

  • The Fighter has been reborn in code: The old imported character and animation models are replaced in production by a 48-part low-poly dark-fantasy oathguard, assembled entirely from reusable geometry, materials, and transforms.
  • A stronger class silhouette: Faceted black iron, crimson cloth, warm brass, a great helm, glowing oath sigil, sword, kite shield, layered plate, gauntlets, greaves, and a moving cloak make the frontline class readable at normal game zoom.
  • The shared humanoid rig is live: Named hips, chest, head, arm, hand, thigh, shin, and cloak pivots drive generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and Death clips for both local and replicated Fighters without changing authoritative movement or combat.
  • Every equipment region has a home: Eighteen named attachment anchors cover head, both shoulders, chest, both gloves, belt, both legs, both feet, neck, both rings, both trinkets, main hand, and off hand, forming the foundation for visible equipped items in the next migration slice.
  • Fighter entry is lighter and more reliable: Five legacy Fighter GLBs no longer appear in the runtime catalog, startup preload, or character factory. Fighter startup now gates only on the nearby Skeleton set, cutting its blocking model requests in half.
  • Pooling and selection stay correct: Reused procedural actors reset their complete pose and scale after death or preview rendering, interaction hitboxes no longer multiply when a mesh changes owners, and nameplates plus party rings use the generated character's declared dimensions.
  • Regression coverage: Unit tests inspect geometry reuse, independent rig state, exact slot anchors, full-height selection, finite bounds, every animation clip, preload removal, and pool reset; hardware-browser evidence renders the Fighter in every state at High and Low quality.

Patch 0.41.0.0 (dark-fantasy foundation and exact world hazards)

  • Eidolon's visual rebirth begins: A single code-driven art manifest now defines the shared dark-fantasy language, palettes, lighting, atmosphere, and hazard identity that every procedural replacement will use.
  • Every region has an identity: Gloamwood Marches, Lanternhold, Moonfrost Expanse, Cinder Wastes, and Stormcrown Reach now use distinct overworld lighting and ambient-particle themes. Thorncrypt, Furnace Below, Shattered Aerie, and Drowned Sanctum have dedicated visual definitions ready for their room-geometry migration.
  • World hazards tell the truth: All 65 live lava pools, sandstorms, lightning fields, and wind gusts now render a themed animated rune boundary whose outer edge exactly equals the server-authoritative damage radius; the old 20% visual overstatement is gone.
  • Danger remains readable on every quality level: Mood particles and ornament can scale down, but exact gameplay boundaries remain visible. Each hazard has its own silhouette, colors, pulse rhythm, and motion language.
  • The migration cannot move backward: A durable art bible, full migration inventory, and automated dependency ratchet record the 106-model legacy baseline and prevent new authored 3D dependencies while the existing payload is replaced patch by patch.
  • Regression coverage: Server tests verify every active hazard's count, type, damage cadence, and replicated radius; client tests verify exact geometry, fallback safety, animation, and cleanup; hardware-browser gallery coverage renders all regional hazards together for visual review.

Patch 0.40.0.1 (ability, synchronization, and interface pass)

  • High-speed movement is smoother: Repeated server acknowledgements for an older accepted input no longer stop newer local prediction or pull the character backward, and slow browser frames can no longer replay more than two simulation ticks in one visible lurch.
  • Movement modifiers stay authoritative: Slow, haste, Swift, crowd-control, charge, teleport, death, and respawn state now reconcile from the server without applying speed changes twice or accepting movement while the character is locked.
  • The world recovers from a bad frame: A transient entity or effect update error no longer terminates the animation loop and leaves the game frozen; stale catch-up work is discarded and rendering resumes on the next frame.
  • Loading cannot be held hostage by unused models: Only the selected character, nearby Skeleton animation set, and playable town base gate entry. Distant enemies, NPCs, summons, and interactive objects load when used, while trees, buildings, camps, and dungeon facades continue through a bounded background phase instead of trapping the loading screen near completion.
  • Dungeon entrances stay available during background loading: Functional overworld portals now load ahead of decorative scenery, and one optional model failure can no longer suppress every dungeon facade or attach stale structures after an instance transition.
  • Remote casts survive on-demand model loading: A nearby player's cast animation is retained while their class mesh finishes loading, and all four class fallbacks now include Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and Death motion instead of remaining frozen after a transient asset failure.
  • Every class ability was audited: All 52 selectable Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric abilities and all 60 rune variants now share validated client/server mana, cooldown, targeting, status, damage, healing, and unlock contracts.
  • Ability results stay in sync: The server now confirms cast mana and cooldown results, broadcasts healing feedback, and restores the complete authoritative cooldown snapshot after reconnect so the hotbar cannot show a rejected ability as ready.
  • AoE visuals match gameplay: Rings, cones, waves, smoke, ground effects, party auras, and projectile impacts now use a shared rune-aware radius registry that mirrors the server's actual hit geometry, including targets whose model extends across the boundary.
  • Spirit Guardians shows its real reach: The aura boundary now renders at 16 metres normally and 24 metres with Expanded Spirits; the boosted form renders at 20 or 30 metres, while the guardians orbit inside that exact damage edge.
  • Projectiles and persistent zones have one authority: Fireball, Meteor, traps, and ground zones now use the replicated server entity for path, impact size, duration, reconnect reconstruction, and removal, preventing duplicate or prematurely hidden effects.
  • Targeting and encounters stay consistent: Hostile targets take click priority over friendly player hitboxes, casts cannot cross instances or select dead targets, and disconnected players are removed from enemy targeting so enemies do not stall on a vanished threat.
  • Combat transitions clear cleanly: Death and respawn validation now ends retained charge, absorb, lethal-prevention, mitigation, healing, owned zones, projectiles, and summons before exercising the real hostile damage path, closing stale-state edges found by the live four-class gate.
  • Chat and character events are separated: The resizable message panel now has Chat and Game tabs. Global and server communication stays in Chat, while loot, XP gains, level-ups, recovery guidance, and reward summaries stay in the private Game log.
  • Menus fit their contents: Inventory, Character, Abilities, Quests, Skill Tree, and Social windows now grow to their useful content size, cap themselves to the active viewport, and scroll internally when the screen is the limiting dimension.
  • Daily quests remain at the quest giver: Optimized movement and combat snapshots no longer mistake protobuf's generated empty quest default for a real quest update. Opening the Quest Giver and resuming a session now reconcile the full authoritative catalog, repair partial legacy quest rows without resetting today's progress, and guarantee the Skeleton starter daily for level-1 characters.
  • Character and Inventory work together: The equipment sheet and inventory can remain open at the same time, sit side by side on wide screens, and recenter correctly when either companion closes.
  • Vendor sell-all covers every equipment slot: Common, Uncommon, and Rare cleanup now includes gloves, necks, and every other equippable slot while continuing to protect gems, materials, Hearts, Shards, and relics.
  • Item stats use a readable scale: Flat Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, Vitality, Damage, and Defense from every equipment slot and gem are reduced 25× (for example, 500 becomes 20). Existing inventory, stash, buyback, equipped, and auction gear migrates once, while percentage effects and item economy values stay unchanged.
  • Regression coverage: Added exact-radius, ability-contract, projectile, cooldown/reconnect, death/respawn, targeting, frame-recovery, movement-smoothness, four-class gameplay, and two-browser multiplayer tests, all verified in the production release gate.

Patch 0.40.0 (entity.go extracted)

  • New module: server/internal/game/entity.go (~950 lines) owns EntityType constants, Quest, Stats, and Entity struct; rune helpers (HasRune, GetRuneForSkill); set-bonus helpers (HasSetBonus, HasAnySetBonus, GetSetBonusValue, HasUniqueEffect); status-effect helpers (GetEffectiveManaCost, ActivateSwiftIfEquipped, GetEffectiveSpeed); RecalculateStats; GetEntityCopy; copyEntity.
  • world.go reduced: 9 325 → 7 444 lines (−1 881); seven duplicate blocks surgically removed.
  • Tests: 932/932 JS green; go build ./... clean.
  • Release confidence: Browser runtimes are now locked and self-hosted, production exposes matching client/server commit identity, and deployment requires database-ready health before live Playwright QA.
  • Real-browser QA: Playwright 1.61.1 covers the anonymous surface plus credential-gated character movement, menus, combat, loot, dungeon transitions, persistence, reconnect, and optional two-account convergence.
  • QA safety: /level now requires an authenticated allowlisted QA username, and tracked load-test credentials were replaced with disposable in-memory generation.
  • Current validation: 951/951 JS tests and all Go packages pass. Current measured hotspots remain above decomposition targets: world.go 8 408, main.go 4 632, GameEngine.js 5 548, and UIManager.js 3 622 lines.

Patch 0.39.3 (Social closeout — QA pass)

  • Regression QA: 932/932 JS tests green; all Go packages pass after the 0.39 decomposition work.
  • DoD note: world.go (9 325 LOC) and main.go (4 542 LOC) exceed the original slice targets (7 500 / 3 500); full reduction is deferred to the 0.40–0.43 architecture decomposition band.

Patch 0.39.2 (SocialPresenceController extracted)

  • New module: src/core/SocialPresenceController.js (108 lines) owns all social / party / friend network-message routing and the local party-highlight state.
  • GameEngine.js reduced: 5 403 → 5 347 lines (−56); setMyPartyId, refreshAllPartyHighlights, sendPartyMessage, kickPartyMember, promotePartyMember, and nine message-handler branches removed from the engine.
  • UIBindings updated: Party action callbacks now route through engine.socialController directly.
  • Tests updated: GameEnginePartyHighlight.test.js rewritten to test SocialPresenceController in isolation; UIBindings.test.js mock updated accordingly.

Patch 0.39.1 (Server handler files extracted)

  • Four new handler files: server/friends_handlers.go (127 lines), server/party_handlers.go (187 lines), server/social_handlers.go (32 lines), server/trading_handlers.go (372 lines) — all package main.
  • main.go reduced: 5 153 → 4 542 lines (−611); handleMessage dispatch switch thinned to 19 single-line delegate calls.

Patch 0.39.0 (social.go extracted)

  • New package file: server/internal/game/social.go (71 lines) — DefaultSocialStatus, validSocialStatuses, NormalizeSocialStatus, SetPlayerSocialStatus, SetPlayerSocialStatusAutomatic.
  • party.go gains GetAllParties: moved from world.go; world.go reduced from 9 394 → 9 325 lines.

Patch 0.38.4 (Friends list and presence — test coverage)

  • DB integration tests: 17 Go tests covering all six friendship CRUD methods; run against a live Mongo instance when MONGO_URI is set, skip cleanly otherwise.
  • Server helper tests: Pure unit tests for usernameToPlayerID, playerIDToUsername, and buildFriendListPayload; DB-gated handler tests for all five MsgFriend* message cases.
  • SocialUI friends tests: 32 JS tests covering friend list rendering, presence updates, incoming request display, tab switching, badge counts, and all four friend callbacks.
  • UIManager toast tests: 16 JS tests covering online-only firing, disabled toggle, per-user rate limiting, 30-second reset, ARIA attributes, localStorage persistence, and _renderFriendToast DOM output.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go and JS test suites for all 0.38 server, UI, and toast surfaces and the 0.38.4 release state.

Patch 0.38.3 (Friend-online toast)

  • A toast appears when a friend comes online: A brief notification slides in at the bottom of the screen showing "username is now online." so you do not have to poll the Social window.
  • Rate-limited per user: The same friend triggers at most one toast every 30 seconds, so rapid reconnects do not spam the screen.
  • Opt-out persists across sessions: Settings exposes a toggle stored as eidolon.friendOnlineToast in localStorage; defaults to enabled.
  • Accessible markup: The toast element carries role="status" and aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce it without interrupting active interaction.
  • Regression coverage: Added UIManager toast coverage for rate limiting, toggle persistence, DOM output, and the 0.38.3 release state.
